title: Enterovirus 2B protein: From viroporin to membrane stress sensor, mechanistic principles of multi-pathway regulation

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Enterovirus 2B protein: From viroporin to membrane stress sensor, mechanistic principles of multi-pathway regulation》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · s0001-p1】The genus Enterovirus within the family Picornaviridae comprises over 250 clinically significant serotypes that circulate worldwide [1–3]. Enterovirus infections manifest with a diverse spectrum of clinical presentations, including upper and lower respiratory tract illnesses, gastroenteritis, hand-foot-and-mouth disease, conjunctivitis, myocarditis, severe neonatal sepsis-like disease, aseptic meningitis, encephalitis, acute flaccid paralysis (AFP), and AFM [3–6]. Important human pathogens within this genus include coxsackieviruses, enterovirus A71 (EVA71), enterovirus D68 (EVD68), echoviruses, and poliovirus (PV) [7–9]. Although these viruses share characteristics such as a small genome, rapid evolution, and broad pathogenic spectrum, targeted antiviral drugs remain absent. The functional pleiotropy of nonstructural protein 2B has emerged as a major obstacle to rational drug design. Understanding how a single ~100-amino-acid protein can engage in such disparate pathways is the central question addressed in this review.

【Introduction · s0001-p2】Enteroviruses possess a single-stranded, positive-sense RNA genome of approximately 7.5 kb in length [10–12]. A single open reading frame encodes a polyprotein that is proteolytically processed into three precursor regions: P1 (structural proteins VP1–VP4) and non-structural regions P2 and P3 [13]. The 2B protein, together with 2A (protease) [14,15] and 2C (helicase/ATPase) [16–18], constitutes the P2 region of the viral genome. Whereas 2A and 3C perform well-defined enzymatic functions, namely the proteolytic cleavage of viral and host targets [19,20], 2B is remarkable for its broad functional repertoire. Understanding how a single ~100-amino-acid protein can engage in such disparate pathways is the central question addressed in this review.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Enterovirus 2B protein: From viroporin to membrane stress sensor, mechanistic principles of multi-pathway regulation》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Rational design of antivirals based on the membrane stress sensor hypothesis · s0008-p1】The pleiotropic roles of 2B in viral replication and pathogenesis make it a compelling target for anti-enterovirus drug development. Existing strategies have largely focused on blocking pore-forming activity and silencing expression. However, none of these studies have targeted the core mechanism proposed here, that is, the ability of 2B to sense the membrane microenvironment and transduce signals through conformational changes. Based on the theoretical framework of the “membrane stress sensor” proposed above, three categories of targeting strategies are presented below. These strategies are schematically summarized in Figure 4.

【Rational design of antivirals based on the membrane stress sensor hypothesis · s0008-p2】The druggability of enterovirus 2B has been substantiated by a growing body of experimental evidence, which can be broadly categorized into channel blockers, oligomerization disruptors, and gene silencing approaches. A comprehensive review by Peng et al. cataloged various small-molecule inhibitors targeting viral ion channels, highlighting the potential of viroporins as antiviral targets. Among these, the anion channel inhibitor DIDS (4,4”-diisothiocyano-2,2”−stilbenedisulfonic acid) has been shown to block the chloride-dependent current mediated by the EV71 2B protein in Xenopus oocytes and, more importantly, to significantly reduce viral titers and cytopathic effects in cell culture [69,101]. Furthermore, a Tat-2B (37–50) peptide, which competitively binds to the H2 transmembrane region, has been shown to inhibit CVB3 infection by interfering with 2B oligomerization [43]. RNA interference approaches have also proven effective, as synthetic siRNAs targeting the 2B coding region of EVA71 markedly reduced viral replication in vitro [42]. Collectively, these studies provide compelling proof-of-concept validation that 2B is a druggable target and that interfering with its channel function, oligomerization, or expression can effectively suppress enterovirus replication.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Enterovirus 2B protein: From viroporin to membrane stress sensor, mechanistic principles of multi-pathway regulation》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusions and outlook · s0010-p1】This study proposes an integrative framework in which the enterovirus 2B protein acts as a “membrane stress sensor,” thereby overcoming the limitations of the traditional viroporin model. Through conformational dynamics, the transmembrane helices of 2B sense changes in the membrane microenvironment (lipid composition, pH, and curvature) and coordinate calcium signaling, cell death pathway selection, and immune evasion outputs in a spatiotemporally specific manner. This framework provides a unified explanation for the direct interactions of 2B with host factors such as Bax, NLRP3, and KPNA1, the functional divergence among different viruses, and the evolutionary footprint of the 2B region as a recombination hotspot.

【Limitations of the viroporin model and the membrane stress sensor hypothesis · s0002-p5】In summary, the existing framework can no longer accommodate the functional breadth and depth of 2B. Studies have shown that the transmembrane helices of 2B can respond with conformational sensitivity to physicochemical parameters, such as membrane lipid composition and pH, with distinct conformational states corresponding to different downstream effector outputs, a characteristic that endows 2B with “sensor” functionality. Therefore, this study proposes a new theoretical framework: defining 2B as a membrane stress sensor, whose diverse functional outputs arise from its conformational responsiveness to changes in the membrane microenvironment. This framework comprises three operational criteria.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Enterovirus 2B protein: From viroporin to membrane stress sensor, mechanistic principles of multi-pathway regulation》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · f0001】Figure 1. Topological model and conformational switch hypothesis of enterovirus 2B protein. (A) type IIB topology of EVA71 2B in the ER membrane. Two helical hairpins (H1 and H2) are connected by a luminal stem-loop, and both termini face the cytosol. Solid lines indicate experimentally validated features: V56 (autophagy induction) and N-terminal Bax-binding domain (aa 22–35). Dashed outlines indicate speculative elements: H53 (putative pH sensor) and C-terminal variable region. (B) membrane microenvironment-driven conformational changes. in the mitochondrial outer membrane (cardiolipin-enriched, high curvature), a “closed” conformation exposes the Bax-binding interface, promoting apoptosis. in the ER membrane or ER-derived vesicles (neutral pH, low cholesterol, low curvature), an “open” conformation exposes a putative NLRP3-binding surface, promoting pyroptosis or immune evasion. The switch is triggered by the lipid composition, pH, and curvature (bidirectional arrow). Dashed outlines indicate speculative elements that are components of the membrane stress sensor hypothesis and await direct experimental confirmation. See the evidence grading section in the main text for a comprehensive explanation of the evidence categories. Note that panel (A) depicts the basal topology of 2B in the ER membrane; it is not intended to represent a specific conformational state. The open/closed conformational switch depicted in (B) is a theoretical model based on indirect evidence, and direct structural validation is required.

【Figure 2. · f0002】Figure 2. Compartment-specific conformations of 2B direct four-cell death pathways. The 2B protein (center) acts as a membrane-embedded sensor, with its functional output dictated by its resident compartment. upper left: at the outer mitochondrial membrane, 2B directly activates Bax, leading to cytochrome c release and caspase-9/3 activation (apoptosis) [32]. upper right: at plasma or ER-derived membranes, the 2B-NLRP3 interaction promotes inflammasome assembly, caspase-1 activation, and IL-1β release (pyroptosis) [33]; K+ efflux is a potential intermediate (dashed arrow). lower left: in a V56-dependent manner [45], CVB3 2B induces LC3-II conversion and autophagosome formation while blocking autophagosome-lysosome fusion, a pH-dependent step in EVD68 presumed to involve disruption of the lysosomal proton gradient [39]. lower right: CVB3 2B promotes the proteasomal degradation of the m6A methyltransferase WTAP, reducing LONP1 mRNA m6A modification and leading to LONP1 accumulation, GPX4 restoration, and suppression of ferroptosis [44]. The mitochondria-associated membranes (MAMs) localization of 2B and the upstream trigger for WTAP degradation (Ca2+ vs direct interaction) remain speculative (dashed lines). Solid arrows, experimentally supported steps; dashed arrows, proposed mechanisms. This figure provides an overview of the four cell death pathways regulated by 2B; each pathway is detailed in Future directions–5.4.

【Figure 3. · f0003】Figure 3. Multilevel regulation of innate immune signaling by the 2B protein. Ca2+ leakage from intracellular stores (bottom) serves as a common upstream trigger for the dual role of 2B in immune evasion. Left, inhibitory pathways: EVA71 2B induces caspase-3 dependent degradation of KPNA1, blocking p-STAT1/2 nuclear translocation and ISG expression [34]. EVA71 2B also binds ILF2, causing its nucleocytoplasmic redistribution and functional inhibition [35]. In EVD68 infection, 2B interacts with the antiviral factor CD74; the virus counteracts this via 3C-mediated CD74 cleavage [36]. right, activating and counter-regulated pathway: viroporin activity of 2B triggers mtDNA release. mtDNA activates the cGAS-STING pathway, leading to TBK1/IRF3 phosphorylation and type I interferon production [84]. This is antagonized by the viral 2C protein, which promotes autophagic degradation of cGAS. The direct link between Ca2+ flux and mtDNA release (dashed line with question mark) remains to be established. Solid lines, confirmed interactions; dashed lines, proposed or indirect connections.
